claims.claim: Mercury sits between commercial compute/RF technology and mission-critical aerospace/defense edge systems; record FY26 backlog above $1.9B and a multi-year 1,000-server BuiltSECURE order support a real secure-processing demand path, while factory automation is being added to improve throughput.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Secure rugged edge-processing integration, U.S.-designed/manufactured motherboard capability and defense qualification create switching friction, but commercial silicon and competing defense integrators limit exclusivity.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Defense modernization supports demand, but program timing and customer procurement concentration make conversion uneven.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Qualification/security requirements raise replacement friction, while alternative qualified embedded-compute suppliers and primes remain substitutes.

risks.risk: Backlog is demand visibility, not guaranteed margin or cash conversion; program timing and execution remain material.

unknowns.unknown: Program-level backlog concentration and cancellation sensitivity remain incompletely disclosed.

claims.claim: FY26 operating recovery is real but not equivalent to normalized earnings quality: FY26 GAAP net loss was $30M while adjusted EBITDA was $150M, and full-year free cash flow fell to $68M from $119M despite record backlog.

factors.name: financialOperatingMomentum
factors.basis: Revenue/bookings/backlog improved strongly, but GAAP profitability and year-over-year cash conversion remain weaker than adjusted operating measures imply.

risks.risk: Adjusted EBITDA growth can overstate economic recovery if working-capital intensity, program charges or cash conversion remain weak.
Defense customer/program concentration and procurement timing can delay backlog conversion.
Commercial compute advances can reduce differentiation unless Mercury sustains security, qualification and integration advantages.

contradictions.claim: Record backlog and stronger adjusted EBITDA coexist with a FY26 GAAP loss and lower full-year free cash flow.
contradictions.resolution: Treat demand recovery as supported while keeping earnings-quality/cash-conversion risk explicit; this is not a present methodology blocker.

unknowns.unknown: The durability of FY27 margin expansion after backlog conversion is not yet observed.
